items.briefing:
There has been a notable surge in email fraud where attackers are exploiting trusted credentials — meaning they use legitimate-looking accounts or services to send convincing scam emails. This makes it harder for staff to spot fake messages, as they may appear to come from known contacts or reputable platforms. Everyone should be extra cautious about unexpected emails requesting actions like payments, password resets, or file sharing, even if the sender looks familiar.

**Practical tip:** Before acting on any unexpected email request — especially involving money or login details — verify it by calling the sender directly using a number you already know.

featured.title: Attackers exploit trusted credentials in email fraud surge
featured.quote: Email fraud now tops incident types at 45%, directly threatening Australian businesses and employees.
